title: Permutation and subsequence regularity
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $f_1,\dots,f_r$ elements which do not generate the unit ideal. Every permutation of the family is regular iff every order-preserving subsequence is regular.

source.place: the induction argument in Stacks Algebra Tag 07DW

proof.text: For the forward implication, extend any sublist l to a permutation l ++ tail using List.Sublist.exists_perm_append. Its weak regularity restricts to the prefix l by isWeaklyRegular_append_iff. Its nonvanishing condition restricts to l because Ideal.ofList (l ++ tail) is the supremum of the two generated ideals. This proves regularity of every sublist.

Prove the two-element weak-regularity swap for any R-module M: if [a,b] is weakly regular and b is regular on M, then [b,a] is weakly regular. Apply Mathlib IsWeaklyRegular.prototype_perm to the swap. Every two-element subpermutation of [a,b] has an empty remaining tail; its second element is either a or b, both regular on M. The quotient by the empty generated ideal is linearly equivalent to M, so its torsion submodule is zero and the prototype permutation side condition holds.

For any R-module M, prove by induction on List.Perm s t that weak regularity of every sublist of s implies weak regularity of every sublist of t. In the cons step, a sublist either omits the common head a, or retains it; in the latter case use regularity of a and apply the induction hypothesis on QuotSMulTop a M. In the swap step s = b::a::rest and t = a::b::rest, sublists retaining at most one head are already sublists of s. For sublists retaining both, split off [b,a] with isWeaklyRegular_append_iff, swap it using the preceding two-element argument and the singleton [a] hypothesis, and transport regularity of the tail across the equality of the ideals generated by [a,b] and [b,a]. The transitivity step composes the two induction hypotheses.

For the reverse implication, apply the preceding permutation induction on the module R, and then take the entire permuted list as its own sublist. This gives weak regularity. A permutation preserves the generated ideal, so the assumed properness of Ideal.ofList (List.ofFn f) supplies the nonvanishing condition. Here ideal scalar multiplication of the top ideal is multiplication by the top ideal, hence equals the ideal itself.

For rs = [a,b], rs' = [b,a], M = R the side condition reduces (rs'' = [], M ⧸ ⊥ ≅ M) to torsionBy R R b = ⊥ and torsionBy R R a = ⊥, i.e. b and a regular on R (isSMulRegular_iff_torsionBy_eq_bot, IsSMulRegular.lean:132); the top_ne_smul part of IsRegular (line 146) transfers since Ideal.ofList [b,a] = Ideal.ofList [a,b].
